marginal_heading: Dishonour of Cheque for Insufficiency of Funds in the Accounts
text: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person for the discharge of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient or exceeds the arrangement, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall be punished with imprisonment for a term up to two years, or with fine up to twice the amount of the cheque, or both. Proviso: Cheque presented within validity, legal demand notice within 30 days of memo, and drawer fails to pay within 15 days of notice.

marginal_heading: Presumption in Favour of Holder (Rangappa v. Sri Mohan)
text: It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability. The Supreme Court in Rangappa v. Sri Mohan (2010) and Kalamani Tex (2021) established that the presumption includes the existence of a legally enforceable debt, shifting the evidentiary burden onto the drawer to raise a probable defence on preponderance of probabilities.

marginal_heading: Offences by Companies & Vicarious Liability of Directors (SMS Pharmaceuticals)
text: If the person committing an offence under section 138 is a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence. As held in SMS Pharmaceuticals v. Neeta Bhalla and Sunita Palita (2022), specific averments must be pleaded in the complaint showing how the accused director was in charge and responsible for company operations.

marginal_heading: Power to Direct Interim Compensation up to 20% of Cheque Amount
text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure / BNSS, the Court trying an offence under section 138 may order the drawer of the cheque to pay interim compensation to the complainant: (a) in a summary trial or summons case, where he pleads not guilty; and (b) upon framing of charge in other cases. The interim compensation shall not exceed twenty per cent of the amount of the cheque, payable within sixty days. In Rakesh Ranjan Shrivastava v. State of Jharkhand (2024), the Supreme Court held Section 143A is discretionary and not mandatory.

marginal_heading: Power of Appellate Court to Order Deposit of Minimum 20% of Fine/Compensation
text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure / BNSS, in an appeal by the drawer against conviction under section 138, the Appellate Court may order the appellant to deposit such sum which shall be a minimum of twenty per cent of the fine or compensation awarded by the trial Court. The deposit shall be made within sixty days from the date of the order, extendable by a further period not exceeding thirty days on sufficient cause (Surinder Singh Deswal v. Virender Gandhi).

act_title: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act)
marginal_heading: Liability of Buyer to Pay within 45 Days & Compound Interest at 3x RBI Bank Rate
text: Section 15 mandates that where any supplier supplies goods or renders services to any buyer, the buyer shall make payment on or before the agreed date, which in no case shall exceed forty-five days from the day of acceptance. Section 16 provides that where the buyer fails to make payment, the buyer shall, notwithstanding anything in any agreement, be liable to pay compound interest with monthly rests to the supplier at three times of the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India.

act_title: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act)
marginal_heading: Reference to MSEFC Statutory Arbitration & Mandatory 75% Pre-deposit to Challenge Award
text: Section 18 overrides arbitration agreements between parties by providing statutory reference to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC) for conciliation and arbitration (Silpi Industries v. Kerala SRTC). Section 19 mandates that no application for setting aside any decree or award made by MSEFC shall be entertained by any court unless the appellant buyer deposits seventy-five per cent of the award amount with the court.

marginal_heading: Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement (Mandatory Bar - Patil Automation)
text: A suit, which does not contemplate any urgent interim relief under this Act, shall not be instituted unless the plaintiff exhausts the remedy of pre-institution mediation in accordance with such manner and procedure with the Legal Services Authority. The Supreme Court in Patil Automation Pvt. Ltd. v. Rakheja Engineers (2022) held that Section 12A is mandatory, and plaints instituted without exhausting pre-institution mediation or seeking urgent interim relief must be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 CPC.

act_title: Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 (RDB / DRT Act)
marginal_heading: Application to the Debts Recovery Tribunal (DRT) for Debt Recovery Exceeding ₹20 Lakhs
citation: Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993, Sec. 19
text: Where a bank or a financial institution has to recover any debt from any person exceeding the statutory pecuniary threshold (₹20 Lakhs under current notification), it may make an application to the Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the branch is situated or the defendant resides or carries on business. The DRT exercises exclusive jurisdiction, barring the jurisdiction of Civil Courts under Section 18.

act_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (SEBI Act)
marginal_heading: Powers of SEBI to Issue Directions, Impound Illicit Proceeds, and Restrain Market Access
text: SEBI is empowered to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of the securities market. Under Section 11B, SEBI may issue directions to any intermediary or person associated with the securities market, including debarring them from accessing the capital markets, restraining directors, impounding and retaining proceeds of fraudulent or unfair trade practices (FUTP), or disgorging illicit profits.

marginal_heading: Prohibition on Dealing in Foreign Exchange & Penalties up to Thrice the Sum Involved
text: Section 3 prohibits dealing in or transferring any foreign exchange or foreign security except through an authorized person. Section 13 provides that if any person contravenes any provision of FEMA, rules, or RBI regulations, he shall be liable to a penalty up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where quantifiable, or up to two lakh rupees where not quantifiable, and continuing penalties up to five thousand rupees every day.
